EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The past 24 hours saw significant escalation in the Middle East, primarily marked by Israel's confirmed assassination of Mohammed Odeh, the newly appointed head of Hamas's military wing, in Gaza, and the declared deepening of Israeli ground operations in Southern Lebanon, accompanied by widespread evacuation warnings. Concurrently, US military action in the Strait of Hormuz targeting Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) speedboats attempting to lay mines, alongside Iranian claims of downing a US drone and firing upon an F-35 jet, underscore severe tensions in the Gulf.

IRAN
Military operations in and against Iran included US strikes on IRGC assets in the Strait of Hormuz. US intelligence identified suspicious Iranian movements, including attempts by IRGC light boats to lay mines, the launch of attack drones towards US ships enforcing a naval blockade, and readiness for missile launches in the 24 hours prior to US attacks. The US military reported sinking two IRGC speedboats in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday night (May 26) for attempting to lay mines and detected activity at Iranian surface-to-air missile sites. Iran’s Foreign Ministry stated the US violated a ceasefire and vowed to respond. Iranian television displayed wreckage it claimed was from a US MQ-9 drone downed in the Strait of Hormuz, with the IRGC claiming to have shot down an MQ-9 and fired upon an F-35 stealth fighter jet that allegedly violated Iranian airspace. The IRGC Navy affirmed full control over the Strait of Hormuz, reporting 25 commercial vessels transited under its security coordination in the past 24 hours, warning of "crushing blows" for any violations. CENTCOM, however, denied resuming "Project Freedom" or escorting ships. Iran executed Gholam-Reza Khani Shakarab, convicted of spying for Israel.

Internally, internet connectivity was reportedly restored across Iran after 87-88 days of widespread disruption, following an order by President Masoud Pezeshkian, though reports indicated potential judiciary efforts to halt the full restoration. Pezeshkian engaged in calls with regional leaders, advocating for Muslim unity. Majtaba Khamenei, the Supreme Leader, issued a message stating the US would no longer have safe havens in the region and predicted Israel's demise within 25 years. Discussions for a potential agreement with the US continue, with Iran demanding the release of $24 billion in frozen funds, half immediately and the remainder within 60 days. Kazakhstan offered to assist in resolving the nuclear program situation.

ISRAEL
Israeli military operations were characterized by targeted assassinations and escalating activity in Lebanon. The IDF and Shin Bet officially confirmed the assassination of Mohammed Odeh, identified as the new head of Hamas’s military wing and an architect of the October 7 massacre. The strike in Gaza City's Rimal neighborhood reportedly killed Odeh, his wife, two sons, and a daughter, with his body found dismembered. A second helicopter strike 20 minutes later critically injured a field commander in Hamas's intelligence mechanism. Defense Minister Katz reiterated Israel’s commitment to eliminating all responsible for the October 7 attacks and preventing Hamas’s military and civilian control in Gaza, also referencing a "voluntary migration plan" from Gaza.

In Lebanon, Israel initiated ground operations beyond the "yellow line" and announced a "deepening" of military activities, including taking controlling territories and fortifying the security strip. Evacuation warnings were issued for numerous villages in the Tyre and Nabatieh areas, and the city of Nabatieh itself, in Southern Lebanon, as well as Mashghara and Sukhmour in the Southern Bekaa Valley, ahead of anticipated IDF attacks. The IDF reported killing a Hezbollah operative who operated and collected a UAV in Southern Lebanon, and attacking over 100 Hezbollah terror infrastructures and operatives in Bekaa and Southern Lebanon overnight. The Home Front Command implemented a new early warning system for rocket and missile fire from Lebanon. Politically, coalition discussions are underway for a bill to dissolve the Knesset, with elections tentatively set between September 8 and October 27. Prime Minister Netanyahu held a phone call with US President Trump and sought to shorten his trial testimony due to "political and security matters." The committee for senior appointments re-approved Roman Gofman as the next Mossad chief despite internal opposition. Former Chief Military Prosecutor Tali Yerushalmi was dismissed from the IDF.

GAZA & WEST BANK
The primary development was the assassination of Mohammed Odeh, the new commander of Hamas's military wing, in Gaza City. Hamas confirmed his death and stated that the ongoing deadly attacks disregard mediation efforts. Reports indicated several killed or injured in a vehicle strike in Mawasi, Khan Younis, and IDF strikes east of Jabalia camp. The IDF also reported destroying 11 kilometers of Hamas terror tunnels in Beit Hanoun. Hamas stated that Israel continues to keep Gaza crossings closed during Eid al-Adha and that Israel's insistence on an "orange line" policy would destroy any ceasefire agreement. In the West Bank, the IDF killed an operative throwing stones in Jenin refugee camp and arrested Shadi Jamaa in Qalqilya, who was involved in a 2007 shooting attack. Israeli settlers were reported to have set fire to a vehicle in Khirbet Masoud.

LEBANON
Escalation intensified significantly, with Israel declaring deepening military operations and deploying ground forces beyond the "yellow line." The IDF issued extensive evacuation warnings for the city of Nabatieh and numerous villages in Southern Lebanon, including 15 villages in the Tyre area and 13 villages in Tyre and Nabatieh, as well as Mashghara and Sukhmour in the Southern Bekaa Valley, anticipating IDF attacks. Israeli airstrikes targeted Sohmor in Western Bekaa and multiple civilian homes in Nabatieh. The Lebanese Health Ministry reported 31 people killed and 40 injured in Israeli airstrikes across Southern Lebanon in the past 24 hours, including women and children. Hezbollah claimed to have conducted 32 military operations against Israeli forces, including using explosive drones against an Israeli military vehicle in Bint Jbeil, Merkava tanks in Rashaf, and an Iron Dome platform in Northern Occupied Palestine. Red Alerts were activated in Kiryat Shmona and surrounding Israeli areas due to missile launches from Lebanon, with one missile falling in an open area, causing no casualties. Aoun continued contacts to prevent wider conflict, with Beirut and Dahieh designated neutral zones.

SYRIA & IRAQ
The Syrian government announced it had located remains of the Assad regime's chemical weapons program and arrested 18 officials, including former military personnel. Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB) chief warned that Western intelligence agencies are planning to use Daesh affiliates in Syria as a proxy force against Iran. In diplomatic developments, Iraq’s National Security Advisor, Qasem Al-Araji, met with Iran’s Deputy SNSC, Ali Bagheri, in Moscow to discuss regional stability and diplomatic solutions to conflicts, with Al-Araji reiterating Iraq's constitutional stance against its territory being used for attacks on neighbors. Iraqi cities, including Karbala and Najaf, observed Eid al-Adha prayers.

GULF STATES
Gulf states, including Saudi Arabia and Qatar, conveyed to Politico that there would likely be no new additions to the Abraham Accords despite demands from former US President Trump, viewing such demands as a "poison pill" without commitment to a Palestinian state. Qatar is actively mediating between the US and Iran regarding the potential agreement on frozen funds, with its Prime Minister and Foreign Minister engaging in calls with Saudi and Jordanian counterparts to discuss mediation efforts. Qatar's Foreign Ministry spokesperson denied reports that Qatar offered $12 billion to Iran for the agreement, calling them baseless attempts to undermine diplomatic efforts. A tanker reported an internal explosion near Muscat, Oman, categorized as an "attack," though no casualties were reported, and the vessel continued its voyage. Saudi Arabia announced a significant urban cooling project for Riyadh by 2027 to reduce temperatures by 8-15 degrees Celsius. Russia’s envoy to the UN warned Gulf states that they are "hostages" to US policy in the Middle East.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Hamas Military Leader Assassinated:** Mohammed Odeh, the new head of Hamas’s military wing and an architect of the October 7 attacks, was assassinated in an Israeli airstrike in Gaza City, along with his wife and children.
2.  **Escalation in Lebanon:** Israel declared deepening military operations in Southern Lebanon, including ground operations beyond the "yellow line," and issued extensive evacuation warnings for Nabatieh and surrounding areas.
3.  **Hezbollah Operations:** Hezbollah claimed 32 military operations against Israeli forces, including the use of explosive drones against Israeli military vehicles and an Iron Dome platform.
4.  **Strait of Hormuz Tensions:** The US military sank two IRGC speedboats attempting to lay mines in the Strait of Hormuz, while Iran claimed to have shot down a US MQ-9 drone and fired upon an F-35 jet.
5.  **Internet Restored in Iran:** After 87-88 days, internet connectivity was reportedly restored across Iran, although some judiciary actions indicated potential internal resistance to the full reopening.
6.  **Iran-US Negotiations:** Indirect negotiations between Iran and the US are ongoing, mediated by Qatar and Pakistan, primarily focusing on Iran's demand for the immediate release of $12 billion of its $24 billion frozen assets.
7.  **Gulf States on Abraham Accords:** Gulf states, including Saudi Arabia and Qatar, indicated reluctance to join new Abraham Accords without a clear commitment to a Palestinian state, despite US pressure.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks are critically high in Southern Lebanon, with Israel’s expanded ground operations and Hezbollah's sustained drone and missile activity. The Strait of Hormuz remains an active flashpoint, with US strikes on IRGC assets and Iranian counter-claims and warnings raising the potential for direct confrontation. Gaza faces ongoing Israeli military pressure following the assassination of a key Hamas commander. Israel's military posture has shifted to more aggressive and deeper operations in Lebanon, indicated by ground incursions beyond the "yellow line" and widespread evacuation orders. The US military posture in the Gulf is assertive, demonstrating willingness to act against perceived Iranian threats. Red lines are being tested by both Iran and the US in the Strait of Hormuz, and Israel's actions in Lebanon signal a potential redefinition of its engagement policy with Hezbollah, possibly pushing against previously understood limits.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **US** maintained an assertive posture, conducting strikes against Iranian assets in the Strait of Hormuz, though CENTCOM denied resuming commercial vessel escorts. President Trump held a phone call with Israeli PM Netanyahu and rescheduled a cabinet meeting to the White House to discuss Iran and the economy. The Justice Department also sued UCLA over alleged antisemitism. **Gulf States** remain cautious, with Saudi Arabia and Qatar expressing reluctance to join new Abraham Accords without a Palestinian state commitment. Qatar actively mediates between the US and Iran over frozen funds, while Russia warned Gulf states they are "hostages" of US policy. **EU members** expressed concern, with Germany's Der Spiegel reporting planned US reductions in military contributions to NATO allies, potentially increasing pressure on European defense. The EU summoned Russia's Chargé d'Affaires over threats. The **Russian** FSB warned of Western plans to use Daesh against Iran, and its UN envoy was denied a US visa. **China** urged dialogue for a resolution in US-Iran talks and suggested a US-Israel-Iran war-end agreement be presented to the UNSC for international legitimacy. **Turkey** pledged full support for Iran-US negotiations. **Pakistan** proposed a five-point plan for peace in the Gulf and Middle East in coordination with China.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Significant contradictions emerged regarding the Strait of Hormuz, with the Wall Street Journal reporting a resumption of US Navy ship guidance ("Project Freedom") which CENTCOM explicitly denied. Reports on internet restoration in Iran were also complex, with the judiciary reportedly issuing a stop order on a related resolution, even as widespread connectivity returned, possibly indicating internal power struggles or delayed implementation. Unverified claims from sources like "omid dana" regarding extensive US strikes on Iranian mainland cities (Bandar Abbas, Andimeshk, Qom, Esfahan, Babolsar) and IRGC suicide drone attacks on US ships lack corroboration from other sources and appear highly biased. Propaganda indicators are evident in reports from Press TV (pro-Iranian regime narratives, critical of US/Israel) and "omid dana" (pro-war, anti-regime framing). Reporting gaps persist regarding the full extent of casualties and damage from Strait of Hormuz incidents and the precise scope and implementation of Israel's "deepening" ground operations in Lebanon. The term "ceasefire" is used by both Iranian and Israeli sources, but its practical application and alleged violations appear to be interpreted subjectively, suggesting a de facto rather than formalized agreement.
